lastText: The Campaign EndsThe AccountNew Ending Found · 1 / 16STRANGER TAKEN FROM THE ICE BY AN ENGLISH SHIP; HIS ACCOUNT TO BE WRITTEN DOWNHe is found on the pack ice at the end of the season, days behind a sledge he has lost sight of, so wasted that the first mate takes him for a body laid out to be buried. Before he will come aboard he asks where the ship is bound. When he is told, he comes. In the cabin, over many nights, the captain writes down what he is told and changes nothing. By the last of it the stranger is too weak to leave the berth. The captain is left with the notebooks, a name he has promised not to use, and the habit of looking north at night, where something is certainly waiting, and certainly in no hurry. The accounts that circulate longest are the unkind ones: a shape glimpsed doing exactly the kind of harm its maker taught it, indifferent to whether the harm was ever asked for.
